key_insight: AURORA-AI is a closed-loop controller that adaptively reallocates compute across AI models to maximize a fairness-aware utility while staying stable under drift and disruption.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical orchestration strategy for deploying human-centric AI systems that must balance accuracy, latency, cost, robustness, interpretability, and demographic fairness in changing environments.
method: Uses Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman feedback control for adaptive resource allocation.
Monitors stability with Lyapunov-based criteria to keep operation resilient.
Optimizes a composite utility that jointly includes predictive performance, parity, cost, latency, robustness, and interpretability.
evidence_signal: In stress-rich discrete-time simulations with demographic bias shocks, concept drift, and black-swan disruptions, AURORA-AI outperformed Static, Round Robin, Greedy, LinUCB, and PPO, achieving faster recovery and better tail utility and fairness metrics.
watch_item: The framework is evaluated in simulation, so real-world gains may depend on how well the utility weights, stability assumptions, and disruption models transfer to deployed systems.
paper_title: Adaptive Utility driven Resource Orchestration for Resilient AI (AURORA-AI)
